chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: Lonnie Simmons gets him the Yeah Man job
summary: His school friend Lonnie Simmons, a tenor man from Mount Pleasant, got him the job in a trio with pianist Eric Henry.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And probably you'd heard they needed a banjo, or something, at Yeah Man, or someone you knew told you, or what?
Well, there was a friend of mine -- Do you know of Lonnie Simmons ?
Saxophone, and [crossed out: all the] organ.
He and I were real close, you know, like -- he being from the same city. He's from right across the way from -- in Charleston -- right across the bridge -- a little town called Mount Pleasant.

Mount Pleasant -- that's where he's from. But, he went to school in Charleston, see? And, I remember him from school. In other words, -- we went to the same school together. Okay -- to bring you up to date -- he was working with the Nighthawks. He worked with the Nighthawks for awhile. And then he came to New York, and he got this job at the Yeah Man. And, he knew about me, you know. He got me the job over there. And I worked over there with him for awhile, and then we left from there and went to a club called the Exclusive Club, which was on --
How many were there at this Yeah Man Club?
It was only the three of us.
Henry -- the piano, and the saxophone.
Well, what kind of sax was [handwritten: Lenrie] playing then?
I thought maybe you might be a vocalist, also.
